constants.name: SEVERITY_WEIGHTS
constants.source: Engineering heuristic — EMC risk scoring weights (CRITICAL=15, HIGH=8, MEDIUM=3, LOW=1, INFO=0). Design choice, not datasheet value.

deterministic.source: Self-evident: full weight for deterministic (rule-output) confidence values — same confidence as datasheet-backed because rules encode deterministic logic over sourced data.

datasheet-backed.source: Self-evident: full weight for first-hand datasheet-sourced confidence values.

heuristic.source: Self-evident: half weight for heuristic (pattern-match / guess) confidence. Standard practice in EMC confidence aggregation; see Ott EMC Engineering (Wiley 2009) §1.3 on source-hierarchy weighting.

constants.name: SWITCHING_EFFICIENCY

switching.source: Engineering default, not a datasheet value: generic switching-regulator efficiency when no datasheet curve is available. Method = ON Semi AND8338 / ADI ADP5023 datasheet: P_loss = P_out*(1-eta)/eta at the worst-case point (min Vin, max Iout); datasheet front-page peaks for corpus-common parts (local datasheets/: TPS5430 95%, LMR33630 >95%, AP63203 88% light-load, MT3608 97%, TPS61023 94%, XL6009 94%, AP3012 81%, TPS63070 95%) sit 5-12 points above worst-case curves, so 85% is a conservative mid-range prior (NXP support guidance: switchers usually 80-90%). Output carries pdiss_confidence=heuristic and the eta in pdiss_source.

constants.notes: Checklist 11b 2026-10-23: only the 'switching' entry is reachable — detect_power_regulators emits topology in {LDO, switching, charge_pump, ic_with_internal_regulator, unknown} and never buck/boost/buck-boost (those live in power_dissipation.sub_topology, which analyze_thermal ignores), so corpus thermal outputs use 85% for all 432 switching_reg entries. The buck/boost/buck-boost keys are dead and disagree with the schematic detector's inline defaults (signal_detectors.py:2226-2245: buck 0.85 / boost 0.80 / buck-boost 0.78, unregistered literals). Filed as KH-469; the three dead entries stay unverified until the tables are unified.
